title: Canary scripting and ops cheatpad (working) - tactical scripts and comms
content:
Purpose:
Short working cheatpad for on-call/runbook-friendly canary scripting and comms. Focused on small-batch LLM rollouts where we need quick ops steps + safe fallback. This is intentionally terse — use during rehearsals and handoffs.

Scope:
- Canary activation and quick rollback scripts for hosted + dedicated routing
- Slack comms templates for stewards and SRE to announce, pause, revert
- Minimal observability checklist (metrics to watch + thresholds)
- Rehearsal steps and post-check items

Quick glossary (ops lingo):
- steward: product teammate owning the slice for the wave
- steward-sla: 15m response window for canary anomalies
- slice: cohort of traffic (percent, org, region)

Activation script (example CLI pseudo):
1) validate artifacts
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    https://console.redwood.ai/api/models/validate?model=v3-canary 
2) open canary slice (10%):
  redwoodctl rollout create --model=v3-canary --slice="10%:random" --policy=gradual --owner=@priya
3) observe for 10m, then escalate or increase

Fast rollback (single command):
  redwoodctl rollout revert --id=<rollout-id> --reason="auto-fallthrough or steward revert"

Slack templates (steward -> #canary-watch):
- Start message: "Starting canary: model=v3-canary slice=10% owner=@priya. Monitoring latency, error-rate, hallucination-rate. Steward SLA 15m. Runbook: <link>."
- Pause request (anyone): "PAUSE canary <id> — observed spike in error-rate (threshold breach). Steward @priya please confirm."
- Revert announce: "Reverting canary <id> -> baseline v2 due to sustained signal: error-rate > 3% and semantic-drift > 0.15. Follow-up: postmortem assigned."

Observability quick-check (min set):
- latency_p95_tokens (route specific) — threshold: +50% relative to baseline for >5m -> alert
- request_error_rate (5xx and model-validation fails) — threshold: >3% sustained for 5m -> hold
- hallucination_score_delta (automated eval) — threshold: >0.12 vs baseline -> investigate
- token_cost_variance — threshold: +40% unit cost -> pause and check batching/quantization
- auth-failures / 403 spike -> immediate stop and security contact

Suggested automated fence (simple heuristic):
- If latency_p95 > 1.5x baseline AND error_rate > 2% for 3 consecutive 1m windows => auto-pause
- If hallucination_score_delta > 0.2 for 10m => auto-revert
(These are conservative; adjust per workload)

Human-run checklist (first 30m):
- t=0: announce in #canary-watch, link to runbook and telemetry
- t=2m: confirm synthetic probes passed (end-to-end smoke tests)
- t=5m: steward sanity check on high-traffic slices (errors, client complaints)
- t=10m: metrics pass? if yes, consider staged increase to 25%
- t=30m: post brief note on health; if any unresolved anomalies, keep paused and escalate to SRE

Rehearsal script (recommended weekly):
- Run through activation + pause + revert on staging with mock telemetry (use controlled failure injection)
- Time metrics: track time-to-pause and time-to-revert; goal < 10m combined

Communication playbook (who to ping):
- steward (product) — primary decision maker for canary actions
- SRE — execute reverts and ensure infra health
- On-call model engineer — check model-specific logs and KV cache issues
- Support triage channel — surface customer-facing incidents

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to unify hallucination_score across different model families? (Lucia investigating eval harness)
- Should we add automated rollback for cost anomalies? (Marcus to prototype threshold rule)
- Need a tiny UI affordance in Console: one-click pause + annotated reason (PR 318 is a start)

Postmortem checklist (if revert):
- capture: request ids, sample inputs from window, model outputs, token counts
- store a snapshot: rollout config + route policies + kernel/quant settings
- quick root-cause hypotheses: infra (GPU/mem), model regression, routing misconfig
- follow-up actions: test-suite update, eval prompt added to regression set, playbook tweak

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep templates short; long playbooks get ignored during incidents
- We must rehearse with regional slices (APAC latency patterns are different)
- Consider a baked-in "safety slice" (0.1% always routed through conservative small-model fallback)

Appendix: short checklist cards for the on-call phone tree
- Card A (start): Announce -> validate smoke -> watch 10m -> escalate if threshold
- Card B (pause): Pause -> collect artifacts -> escalate to steward -> run revert if confirmed
- Card C (revert): Revert -> confirm baseline traffic restored -> file postmortem

If helpful, I can convert this into a condensed runbook card that fits the SRE on-call Slack workflow.

End of cheatpad.
